baseline.note: Protocol-matched baseline = paper's 3DGS-dagger row (same hyper-parameters + neural colour renderer, no depth passes): 16.46 PSNR / 0.440 SSIM / 0.401 LPIPS. Compare our gain with the paper's +2.66 dB (19.12 vs 16.46).

llff-fewview3-r8-dng._doc: DNGaussian 3-view LLFF (official scripts/run_llff.sh): images/ (hard links) and transforms.json (byte copy) of llff-fewview3-r8 (same split: test = every 8th sorted image, train = 3 uniform np.linspace+round of the rest, val = unused; 504x378 PIL bicubic /8). Differs from llff-fewview3-r8 in init and sidecar: points.npz = official --rand_pcd (np.random.seed(0); uniform box from the bbox of the FULL LLFF sparse/0/points3D.bin: int(max extent*50) points in [20th-smallest, +1.3 extent]); dng_depth.npz = MiDaS v3 DPT_Hybrid (dpt_hybrid_384.pt, sha256 501f0c75...) depth of the 3 TRAINING views only (official get_depth_map_for_llff_dtu.py: full-res -> dpt_transform -> bicubic to H/8xW/8 -> uint16 min-max; target 255 - png/255), keyed by the native viewmat, plus the official 180-pose spiral camera centres (CreateLLFFSpiral) for near-camera pruning. Built by reproductions/dngaussian/tools/prepare_dng_llff.py (PYTHONPATH=~/models/dpt/pylib for timm 0.6.12, MiDaS repo in ~/models/dpt/midas_repo); NOT rebuildable by bench.py prepare.

notes: --steps must be 6000 (= density total_steps: final clean_views + bake); any multiple of 1000 bakes for ss-eval. First use JIT-compiles the CUDA encoders (~3 min, cached in ~/.cache/torch_extensions). ~0.2 s/step on a busy shared A6000 => ~20 min per scene; peak memory ~0.3 GB. Uses the depth sidecar via ss-train --data (bench.py passes it). No per-scene numbers exist (paper, supp., README), so the comparison is the 8-scene average. Official README: PSNR unstable across runs (random init); consider 2-3 seeds via --extra '--seed N' if GPU time allows.
